name: Chaos and Order
_what: Info film for the Chaos/Order domain: the Churnfolk, the Enginewrights and the Lattice-Cities, the wild/ordered nanite quarrel, the two courts of the Churn, and the room on no plan.

lines: Between chaos and order runs a long road.
At one end nothing keeps its shape. At the other, nothing is unplanned.
Under both ends runs the same nanite, in two states.
Ordered, it goes where it is put. Wild, it thrives in the gaps nobody keeps.
The Churnfolk break ordered nanite back to wild. The Enginewrights order the wild again.
Nobody calls it a war. It is an argument about who decides what a place is for.
The Churn Edge.
Things here are mostly reliable, which means they were reliable the last time anyone checked.
The Churnfolk ride luck and read the grain of a thing as it comes apart.
They are best where the plan has stopped working.
Tumbledown has never been in the same place twice.
You can find anything there once. You can never find it twice.
Improvisers thrive where others founder. Riders surf the collapse. Unspoolers break things for the joy of it.
after: None of it works the same way twice.

lines: Cassa Redsail takes ships nobody insures.
She wants one take big enough to stop. She has said that four times.
Deeper in, in the wildest place in the world, there are two courts.
One keeps every promise to the letter, at a price named aloud. You leave richer, and hollowed.
The other will not trade at all.
Urd Stonefast has built the same hall for two hundred years, and rebuilds it each time the Churn takes it, cheerfully.
Pressureholt is a city that is also a machine.
Its people are warm, and it comes out as maintenance: they will mend your boots, your argument and your marriage, unasked.
Chief Kettering keeps the Schedule.
She asks when you will be leaving before she asks your name, and means it kindly.
Enginecraft reads what a mechanism is for, and tells it what to become.
The old doors under the world still half-listen to them.
The Great Engine: a mechanism the size of a mountain range, still running.
Here everything is a machine, including you.
Mechanists mend and command. Deep-Workers make great works that change the maker.
The craft needs a mechanism to talk to. The wild gives it nothing to hold.
Each person he improves becomes a device with a function, and thanks him.
after: He wants a world of perfect mechanisms, people included.

lines: Rethe is becoming the Engine, part by considered part, and still asks to be talked out of it.
That asking is the whole of him.
One floor of one arcology. Work, meals, rest: all planned, all better than you would have chosen.
after: The people will tell you so, and it is true.

lines: Latticework binds possibility down until it is reliably true. What it binds stays bound.
It cannot improvise. Anything that has to grow resists it.
Orderers set things right. Registrars keep the charter and the claim.
Fixers bind a person to the approved possibilities, from outside, without asking.
The Grand Lattice, where order became a faith.
Nothing is unplanned and nothing is free, and the second is the point.
Corvane, the Deep Warden, goes into the old works where no one returns from, and returns.
The lattice shows at their edges now.
Wildcraft rides collapse. Latticework prevents it. Each is strongest where the other is blind.
after: The Lattice spreads its order outward and calls it peace. The Churn is the last place it cannot predict.

lines: Each Reach is leaning harder into its own extreme. The edges of the world are getting sharper.
In the Grand Lattice there is one room on no plan. Nobody knows who made it.
after: People go there, and come back unable to say what for.

title.line2: The Churn, the Engine, the Lattice
